newsitem.title: USA: Teen arsonist gets community service.
newsitem.headline: Teen arsonist gets community service.

text.p: The North Carolina teenager who set fire to a historic church this summer was sentenced to probation, community service and continued mental health treatment, a prosecutor said Wednesday.

The teenager, a white 13-year-old girl, was arrested shortly after the fire and placed in a mental facility. "She will continue in her residential mental health placement, the same facility she was put in in June," Mecklenburg Assistant District Attorney Reid Chisholm said.
Matthews Murkland Presbyterian Church lost its former sanctuary, built by former slaves in 1864, when the girl set a fire that quickly engulfed the one-room wooden edifice.

Her probation will last a year and community service must total 200 hours, according to Chisholm, who handled the case. There was no fine and the church, which plans to rebuild on the site, did not request restitution, he added.
The crime occurred while federal agents were already investigating a string of arsons at churches primarily attended by blacks across the South.

But authorities say the girl's actions were not motivated by race but were anti-Christian. The girl, whose name was not released because she is a juvenile, apologised to the pastor of the church at a closed court hearing Tuesday.

"We met with her for the first time yesterday and shared with her that we hold no animosity and wish for her the best," said Rev. Larry Hill, pastor of Matthews Murkland. He said the girl's response was warm -- contrary to her previous cold and withdrawn demeanor and appearance.
"She expressed remorse for what she had done. We responded to that as a community of faith needs to and should," he said.
The girl must stay at the mental facility until authorities feel she is ready to function in society.
"The discipline in this instance is aimed at helping her to become a normal, functional human being again. In one sense it's a model for how juvenile offenders can be helped," Hill said.
